Home Paid news feed Foto Agerpres Press Monitoring Bucharest Phone: +4 021.2076.110 Babes-Bolyai University contributes to study on European high-mountain plant extinction rates Category: English Date: 2026-09-05 18:08:49 Foto: Silviu MATEI / AGERPRES Photo A new study published in the journal Science shows that although the total number of plant species on Europe's mountain summits is increasing, this trend masks an acceleration of local extinctions, particularly among species adapted to high-altitude cold environments. The research was conducted by a European consortium including Prof. Mihai Puscas of Babes-Bolyai University (UBB) and Dr. Tudor Ursu of the Institute of Biological Research in Cluj-Napoca. It draws on monitoring data from 896 permanent vegetation plots on 62 mountain summits across 16 European mountain regions, including the Carpathians, surveyed four times between 2001 and 2022 within the GLORIA international network. According to the study, climate warming has enabled lower-elevation plants to move upslope and colonize mountain peaks, increasing overall species richness. At the same time, cold-adapted alpine species are disappearing more frequently, with extinction rates rising fastest on summits that have warmed the most. The Carpathian data reinforce this pattern and highlight the importance of long-term monitoring of the same plant communities. 'Finding more species on mountain summits may seem positive at first glance. In reality, this increase hides a more complex shift: low-altitude plants are moving up, while some characteristic alpine species are declining,' said Prof. Puscas, noting that long-term monitoring in the Rodna Mountains helps capture these processes and understand their implications for the future of mountain biodiversity. The study also shows that local extinctions are often preceded by long periods of population decline. Because alpine plants are typically long-lived and stress-tolerant, their disappearance may occur long after environmental changes begin. The current acceleration of losses may therefore reflect an 'extinction debt' accumulated over recent decades. Researchers warn that an increase in species numbers does not necessarily signal improved biodiversity: new colonisers may mask the loss of the very plants that define alpine ecosystems. UBB Rector Daniel David said that publications in top scientific journals such as Science, alongside major competitive research grants, are key benchmarks for the university's performance. He also congratulated Prof. Puscas for his contribution to the study. https://www.politico.eu/article/us-scold.text: BRUSSELS — U.S. deputy Pentagon chief Elbridge Colby on Tuesday hit out at Ukraine for its long-range strike campaign against Russia — a fresh blow to Kyiv as it seeks to shore up its negotiating position during peace talks with Moscow. His comments, made at a meeting primarily aimed at raising further support for Ukraine, come as the U.S. is expected to hold fresh peace negotiations with Ukraine and Russia in the coming weeks. “While the public conversation focuses on the spectacle of deep strikes designed to incur pain on the Russian population, our assessment is that such strikes have not been effective … nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line,” Colby said at a meeting of the Ukrainian Defense Contact Group defense ministers in Brussels. Advertisement Advertisement “Such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure ... have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate,” he said, adding: “The balance of advantage in deep strikes may well favor Moscow.” The comments prompted an immediate rebuke from Ukraine’s NATO allies. “Criticizing strikes like that in Russia to destroy strategic military … targets is quite a stupid thing,” German Foreign Minister Boris Pistorius said after the meeting. “Instead of criticizing that, we should rather criticize and talk about [Russia’s] terroristic strikes every night.” “It's not for us to tell Ukraine how to fight their war,” U.K. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting told reporters. “In terms of deep strike capability, there's no doubt in my mind that it's helped to degrade [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's war machine.” Ukraine has in recent months stepped up long-range attacks deep inside Russia, targeting depots of the online retailer Wildberries, military facilities, oil refineries and fuel export facilities. It says it has taken out 30% of Russian oil refining capacity. On Tuesday, Ukraine said it had destroyed part of the Kerch bridge linking Russia to Crimea. Washington has long opposed deep strikes against Russia, particularly those that affect oil infrastructure. U.S. President Donald Trump last month accused Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. Zelenskyy has previously said the strikes give Ukraine “equal footing” in negotiations with Russia. Advertisement Advertisement Moscow has also pummeled Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Funding for Ukraine Colby urged ministers to keep funding the NATO-backed PURL program, where Ukrainian allies pay for American weapons for Kyiv. “Sustaining the flow of critical munitions is essential for Ukrainian troops to continue holding the front line,” he said. PURL was set up last year after the U.S. stopped directly funding Ukraine's war effort following Trump's return to power. On Tuesday, several countries including Germany, Norway and Sweden announced over $300 million in fresh contributions to the scheme. The U.K. separately announced £240 million in air defense support, including over 1,000 short-range missiles and a dozen air defense radars. NATO allies are still billions short of meeting a €70 billion alliance military aid target for Ukraine this year, and a separate goal of raising at least €12 billion for PURL. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte told POLITICO he was “cautiously optimistic” allies could still meet the overall target, set at the alliance’s July summit in Ankara. Despite the criticism of long-range strikes, Colby praised Ukraine’s “very effective” use of mid-range strike drones to “deny Russian advances” on the front line. Ukraine last week said it had detected limitations on critical U.S. Starlink satellite services for the second time in two months, a move Kyiv said made it more difficult to intercept Russian drones. Asked about the latest restrictions, Colby demurred, telling reporters: “We are very focused on supporting Ukraine's ability to defend itself and these … mid-range strikes, and we're taking steps that are consistent with that policy.” Advertisement Advertisement

https://hvg.hu/360/20261119_202647-seszt.text: A hazai korrupciós hálózat irdatlan méretére és a dilettantizmusra egyaránt utal az a készpénzmennyiség, amelyre a Seszták-ügyben bukkantak a nyomozók. A HVG-nek nyilatkozó szakértők Unger Anna kommunikációs bakijairól és a pénzmosás lehetséges eszközeiről is beszéltek. Bár az sem éppen mindennapos, hogy a nyomozó hatóság 6,5 milliárd forintnyi, feltehetően állami vagyont szerez vissza, az összeg nagyságánál árulkodóbbnak tartják a HVG-nek nyilatkozó szakértők az összeg formáját, azt, hogy készpénzben, dollárban, euróban és forintban került elő az erdőben elásott, raktárakban elrejtett összeg. Győry Csaba egyetemi adjunktus, az ELTE Jogtudományi Intézetének gazdasági büntetőjoggal és gazdasági bűncselekményekkel foglalkozó kutatója arra emlékeztet, hogy a hazai kriminológiában a készpénzes gyakorlatot a nagyságrendileg kisebb összegű, alacsonyabb politikai vagy igazgatási körökben előforduló „megkenésekhez” kötötték – ahol a pár milliós tételeket hamar el is költhették –, nem az akár miniszteri szintig érő, többmilliárdos ügyletekhez. A most megtalált vagyon szerinte egészen új megvilágításba helyezi azt, hogy mekkora mennyiségű készpénz mozoghatott a magyar korrupciós hálózatokban az utóbbi években. Molnár Csaba ügyvédet, a Nemzeti Nyomozó Iroda pénzmosás elleni részlegének egykori vezetőjét is meglepte, hogy erre a szokatlanul nagy összegre bankjegyekben bukkantak, mert „pénzt mosni ugyan világszerte egyre nehezebb, de azért mindig van, aki megcsinálja, a kérdés csak az ár”. Sárvári Nicholas, a nemzetközi vagyonvisszaszerzés szakértője (aki néhány hónapja a Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatal elnökjelöltjeként vált ismertté) azt mondja a HVG-nek: a munkája során nagyon sok olyan ügyet látott, ahol ehhez fogható csalásokról volt szó, de az „csak a filmekben van”, hogy ekkora összeget készpénzben rejtsenek el.
